quote: and a lot of my neighbors have it.
stewart_read: Neighbor-influence is a strong social-proof reason to act; rep acknowledged generically but didn't reflect it back as leverage.
coaching_implication: Could have said something like 'so you'll be one of the first on your street with it locked in' to use neighbor influence as forward pull.

quote: But, you know, I have a problem with the bill.
stewart_read: Rep treats this purely as a logistics problem (which months to use) rather than an opening to align against the utility ('sounds like Excel's error cost you money you shouldn't owe').
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep genuinely just needed usable data and solved that correctly given the constraint.
coaching_implication: Even solving the practical need, rep could pair it with a one-line emotional bridge tying the billing mess to 'this is exactly the kind of unpredictability solar removes.'

quote: I just got a bill for $584.
stewart_read: This is the single highest-leverage bill-pain moment in the call and it passes with only 'That's a big jump there.'
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read considered: rep may have been focused on securing the kWh data before the customer got frustrated navigating the site — but nothing later reclaims the number for the pitch.
coaching_implication: Should flip immediately: 'That's exactly the kind of bill swing solar locks you out of — let's make sure the closer walks you through how that gets fixed.'

quote: Oh, yeah. I would've been shocked, you know, if I didn't know what this was about.
stewart_read: Customer himself frames the number as shocking, handing the rep the exact emotional cue to flip; rep responds only with logistics ('that'll be perfect to help us... get you a good design started').
coaching_implication: This is the flip line the rep should have used — acknowledge the shock, then tie it to why the appointment matters.

stewart_read: Customer admits difficulty navigating tech; rep reassures lightly ('I'm pretty slow with this stuff too') which is adequate but minimal.
coaching_implication: Handled acceptably — brief, non-condescending reassurance kept momentum without dwelling.

quote: Yeah. I mean, if you have the last three or four that were that were accurate, we we could look at those, and that would still help us out.
stewart_read: Good improvisation on an edge case not in the standard script — rep adapted rather than forcing the standard single-bill ask.
alternative_hypothesis: Not a violation in the negative sense; flagged here as adaptive handling worth noting to the manager as a positive deviation.
coaching_implication: Worth reinforcing as a model response for atypical billing situations on future coaching reviews.

quote: We'll give you a call tomorrow at 9AM.
stewart_read: Recap and time are given but the explicit 'is that fair?' handshake and the no-driving instruction are missing from the confirmed button-up.
coaching_implication: Add the verbal handshake and driving instruction — verified events already show button_up as only 3/4 complete.
